title: Human-Computer Interaction: UI Evaluation Criteria and Methods
summary: Evaluating a user interface involves assessing usability and user experience through various evaluation methods while maintaining safety and ethical standards.

sections.title: 1. Evaluation Criteria: Usability
paragraphs: Usability is about how easy, efficient, and effective a system is to use.
Usability Survey: Often includes questions involving the ease of use, ease of learning, fatigue, simple preference, and other questions specific to the given interface.
list: Quantitative: Measured through performance tasks (e.g., how many clicks, how much time it takes to complete an action).
Qualitative: Based on user opinions, feedback, and surveys (e.g., how simple or tiring the system feels).

sections.title: Evaluation Criteria: User Experience (UX)
paragraphs: UX is more than usability it’s about the overall feeling, satisfaction, and emotional connection users have while interacting with the system. Covers how enjoyable, intuitive, and stress-free the app feels.

sections.title: 2. Evaluation Methods
list: INTERVIEW / OBSERVATION: The simplest way: talk to users or watch them use the system. Helps identify problems that designers might miss.
COGNITIVE WALKTHROUGH: Users "think aloud" while using the system. They describe what they are doing and why. This reveals their thought process and points of confusion.
EXPERT HEURISTIC EVALUATION: Usability experts review the system using established principles called heuristics.

sections.title: Nielsen's Ten General UI Heuristics
list: Match between system and the real world
Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

sections.title: Measurement
paragraphs: Collect numerical or survey-based data to measure effectiveness. Can involve time, error rates, or satisfaction scores.

sections.title: 3. Safety & Ethics
paragraphs: Evaluations must be safe and respectful. Users should give informed consent before participating. Participants should always have the right to stop whenever they feel uncomfortable.

sections.title: Summary
paragraphs: Evaluating a user interface ensures that:
list: The system is easy to use (usability)
The experience is positive and enjoyable (UX)
The process is safe, ethical, and user-centered
